title: The Scraped Knee
briefing: Mateo, 12, skids off his skateboard and scrapes his knee. It bleeds for a few minutes, then stops on its own. A dark crust covers it for a week, and when the crust falls off there is new pink skin underneath.
question: How did Mateo's knee stop the bleeding and fix itself?

clues.title: Slowing by itself
clues.text: The knee bled steadily for the first minute, then slowed and stopped after about five minutes. Nobody pressed on it.
clues.shows: the bleeding switching off by itself within minutes

clues.title: Sticky and dark
clues.text: Before it was even dry, the blood on the scrape turned sticky and dark red, like jelly. The edges looked glued together.
clues.shows: blood thickening into a jelly-like plug

clues.title: Under the bandage too
clues.text: His mom put a bandage on right away. It still stopped in about five minutes, even though no air could reach it.
clues.shows: the plug forming even with no air to dry the blood

clues.title: New skin under the scab
clues.text: A dark crust stayed on for a week. When it fell off there was new pink skin underneath.
clues.shows: the scab protecting the knee while new skin grew

hypotheses.text: Air dries the blood until it stops, like paint drying.
hypotheses.flaw: Paint takes hours to dry and needs air — but the bleeding stopped just as fast under a bandage where no air could reach it.

hypotheses.text: The scrape was not deep enough to really bleed.
hypotheses.flaw: It did bleed, steadily, for several minutes — then something switched it off by itself.

hypotheses.text: Tiny cell pieces in his blood called platelets rushed to the scrape and stuck together, building a mesh that plugged the leak; the plug dried into a scab that protects the knee while new skin grows underneath.

hypotheses.flaw: An infection builds up over days and gets worse; this bleeding stopped in minutes and the knee healed cleanly within a week.

transfer.context: Ana cuts her finger on the edge of a sheet of paper. It bleeds a little, then stops after a couple of minutes, and a thin dark line forms along the cut.
options: Paper is clean, so it can't make you bleed much.
The cold air froze the blood.
Platelets stuck together at the cut and built a plug, which dried into a thin scab.
transfer.retryHint: Bleeding that stops on its own after a few minutes — which of Mateo's clues looked like that?
transfer.explanation: Ana's paper cut is a small version of Mateo's knee. Platelets in her blood stuck together at the cut and built a mesh plug within minutes; the thin dark line is that plug drying into a scab while new skin grows underneath.

takeaway: Your blood carries its own repair kit. Platelets stick together at a cut and build a mesh plug in minutes; the plug becomes a scab that guards the spot while new skin grows underneath.
